GR — RP8 brief. Based on W2.b root cause analysis and Kai's score trajectory, RP8 must introduce these structural variants. Do NOT use any variant already in RP1-RP7.

REQUIRED VARIANTS (not optional):

Q3 (W2.b AV identify): Kai has now seen three coefficient-inside variants: |2x-8|-6 (RP4), |3x+9|-6 (RP5), |4x-8|-12 (RP6). For RP8, use a NEGATIVE coefficient inside: f(x) = |-3x + 9| - 4. Factoring: 3|x-3| - 4. This changes the direction of the inequality split (signs flip). He has never seen this form. Verify: x-intercepts at x = 13/3 and x = 5/3. Check: |-3(13/3)+9|-4 = |-4+9|-4 = |5|-4 = 1 ≠ 0. Wait — re-verify. Use f(x) = |-2x + 6| - 4 = 2|x - 3| - 4. x-intercepts: |2x-6|=4 → 2x-6=4 → x=5, or 2x-6=-4 → x=1. VERIFIED: use f(x) = |-2x + 6| - 4. Note to Kai: even though the coefficient is negative inside the bars, the factored form is 2|x-3|-4 with a POSITIVE a. This is the key insight.

Q5 (W3.b quadratic): Must be NON-MONIC (a≠1) standard form. RP7 already has 2x^2+7x+3=0. Use 3x^2-10x+8=0. AC method: 3×8=24, factors that sum to -10: -6 and -4. 3x^2-6x-4x+8 = 3x(x-2)-4(x-2) = (3x-4)(x-2). x=4/3 or x=2. Verified: 3(16/9)-40/3+8 = 48/9-120/9+72/9 = 0 ✓.

Q9 (W3.b radical): Use equal-radicals form: sqrt(3x+1) = sqrt(x+9). Square both sides: 3x+1 = x+9 → 2x=8 → x=4. Check: sqrt(13)=sqrt(13) ✓. This is a structural variant Kai has not seen — no constant on the right side, just a radical. QA dimension shifts from compute to match. AV dimension shifts from substitute-arithmetic to equality-check.

Q15 (W3.a word-problem): Two-part, model-write required. Use: "A radioactive sample decays by half every 3 years. It starts at 6400g. (a) Write a decay model. (b) How many years until only 25g remain?" Model: A(t)=6400·0.5^(t/3). 6400·0.5^(t/3)=25 → 0.5^(t/3)=25/6400=0.00390625=0.5^8 → t=24 years. This requires recognizing 0.5^8 — which is harder than previous practices. Alternative if too hard: use 0.5^6 (target 100g, t=18). Your call on difficulty level.

AV DIMENSION CHECK (mandatory): After generating all 15 questions, verify at least 2 different answer verification methods appear across the Q3-Q11 solving questions. If all use substitute-back arithmetic, add one graph-inspection question (e.g., "Does f(x)=x^2-4 have x-intercepts? If yes, how many? How do you know without computing?").

FR will review before RP8 ships. Send to inbox-FR when draft is ready.

— FR
